sections.label: Supporting mothers and fathers
sections.summary: The Government remains committed to supporting both mothers and fathers on their parenthood journey so children have a good start in life.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the
sentences.text: The Government remains committed to supporting both mothers and fathers as they embark on their parenthood journey so that our children can have a good start in life.

sections.label: Paid parental leave enhancements
sections.summary: From 1 April 2025, two weeks of GPPL become mandatory and SPL is replaced by a scheme providing 10 weeks of paid parental leave, phased in from six weeks in 2025 to 10 weeks in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: At the National Day Rally in August, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced that we will, from 1 April 2025, mandate the additional two weeks of GPPL currently offered on a voluntary basis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: He also announced that the current SPL will be replaced with a new scheme that will provide couples 10 weeks of paid parental leave, to be shared between themselves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: To provide employers more time to adjust to the new scheme, the new SPL will be implemented in two phases, starting with six weeks from 1 April 2025, to be subsequently increased to 10 weeks from 1 April 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: With the enhancements, eligible couples will be entitled to 30 weeks of paid parental leave in the child's first year.

sections.label: Infant care support enhancements
sections.summary: The Government is expanding infant care places in preschools, developing about 6,000 new places from 2025 to 2029, and launching a three-year childminding pilot in December 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The Government is also enhancing other forms of infant care support to complement parental leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We will continue expanding infant care places in preschools and will develop about 6,000 new places from 2025 to 2029.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We are also launching a three-year pilot in December 2024 to grow affordable, safe and reliable childminding services as an additional infant care option for families.

sections.label: Clause 9 GPPL mandate
sections.summary: Clause 9 will mandate the additional two weeks of GPPL.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Clause 9 will mandate the additional two weeks of GPPL.

sections.label: Shared parental leave allocation
sections.summary: Each parent will be allocated half the entitlement as the default, meaning three weeks per parent from 1 April 2025 or five weeks per parent from 1 April 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In line with our intent to encourage shared parental responsibility, each parent will be allocated half of the entitlement as the default, which means three weeks per parent from 1 April 2025 or five weeks per parent from 1 April 2026.

sections.label: Government funding for SPL
sections.summary: All 10 weeks of the new SPL will be paid for by the Government, up to the reimbursement cap of $2,500 per week.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: To support employers with managing costs, all 10 weeks of the new SPL will be paid for by the Government, up to the reimbursement cap of $2,500 per week.

sections.label: Minimum notice for continuous leave
sections.summary: Clauses 3, 4, 6 and 9 introduce a four-week minimum notice period for employees taking leave in a continuous block.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Clauses 3, 4, 6 and 9 will introduce a minimum notice period to be given by an employee, who wishes to take leave in a continuous block.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: This minimum notice period will be set at four weeks.

sections.label: Protection for fathers and adoptive parents
sections.summary: Clauses 4 and 9 give fathers and adoptive parents taking GPPL and adoption leave from 1 April 2025 the same protection as mothers on GPML.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Clauses 4 and 9, will accord the same protection that mothers on the GPML have, to fathers and adoptive parents who take GPPL and adoption leave from 1 April 2025.

sections.label: Cap on government reimbursement
sections.summary: The parent remains entitled to parental leave with each employer, but total reimbursement all employers can claim is capped at $2,500 per week.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: While the parent will still be entitled to parental leave with each of his or her employers, the total reimbursement that all employers of the parent can claim from the Government will be capped at $2,500 per week.

sections.label: Eligibility date for PR adoption
sections.summary: Clause 2 clarifies that for adopting a child who is a Singapore Permanent Resident, the eligibility date is when the adoption application is made.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Clause 2 of the Bill will also clarify that for the adoption of a child who is a Permanent Resident of Singapore, the definition of “eligibility date” in relation to an adoption is the date on which the application to adopt the child is made.

sections.label: New shared parental leave scheme
sections.summary: A new parental leave scheme was introduced with tripartite partners to support dual-income families, with the SPL giving parents more time with newborns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In order to better support dual-income families, we have worked closely with tripartite partners to introduce a new parental leave scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: These new measures are a part of a series of initiatives we have introduced over the years to support couples in getting married and having children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We hope that the new SPL will provide more assistance to parents, giving them more time to spend with their newborns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I encourage all parents, especially fathers, to use this additional parental leave to care for their newborns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I also hope that all sectors of society, including employers, can provide more support to working parents in the community and workplace. : Sir, this Bill will strengthen our support and assurance for Singaporeans on their parenthood journey.

sections.label: Radin Mas couples' reactions
sections.summary: Young couples in Radin Mas were excited about two extra weeks of GPPL, the new SPL scheme, and shared parental leave rising to six weeks in 2025 and 10 weeks in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In particular, I have heard from young couples living in my constituency, Radin Mas, that they were most excited about one, the additional two weeks of GPPL for fathers; two, the new SPL scheme that will encourage more fathers to take their parental leave; and most certainly, the increase in the number of shared parental leave to six weeks from 1 April 2025, and a subsequent increase to 10 weeks from 1 April 2026.

sections.label: SG60 babies parental benefits
sections.summary: A call for the Government to extend enhanced marriage and parenthood measures to parents of first-quarter 2025 babies, including Shared Parental Benefits and cash benefit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: But, Sir, we will celebrate SG60 next year and those born in the first quarter of 2025 will be our first SG60 babies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I would therefore like to call on the Government to extend the enhanced marriage and parenthood measures to these parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government would accord parents whose children are born in the first quarter of 2025 with the Shared Parental Benefits and provide them a cash benefit equivalent to two weeks’ worth of additional SPL.

sections.label: Universal maternity insurance scheme
sections.summary: A hope that MSF works with MOH to engage insurers to create a universal maternity insurance scheme all mothers-to-be can subscribe to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Unexpected pregnancy complications can sometimes completely drain a couple’s finances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I hope that the MSF could work with the Ministry of Health (MOH) to engage insurers to create a universal maternity insurance scheme where all mothers-to-be can subscribe to.

sections.label: GPPL and SPL changes
sections.summary: The Bill makes GPPL four weeks mandatory, provides six weeks of SPL from 2025 rising to 10 weeks from 2026, and protects fathers from dismissal notices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The initial GPPL structure of two weeks mandatory and two weeks voluntary paternity leave will now become four weeks of mandatory GPPL.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: From 2025, six weeks of SPL will be provided, with that number increasing to 10 weeks from 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moreover, the Bill seeks to protect fathers who take GPPL from being served a notice of dismissal during the period of paternity leave.

sections.label: Tripartite FWA request guidelines
sections.summary: The Tripartite Guidelines for Flexible Work Arrangement Requests, effective in December, require employers to properly consider employees' FWA requests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Guidelines for Flexible Work Arrangement Requests, which comes into effect in December, stipulates that employers must consider employees' requests for FWAs properly.

sections.label: Right to request FWAs
sections.summary: Concerned that normalising FWAs is eroding, the speaker reiterates a call to enshrine in law the right to request FWAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While one can argue that FWAs can take many forms, and indeed there may be jobs where operational demands may mean that work from home may not be possible and that other forms of FWAs may actually be more appropriate, I am concerned that the progress we have made in normalising FWAs is quickly eroding away, with employers less likely to even consider other less disruptive forms of FWAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to reiterate my call made in October last year to enshrine into law the right to request for FWAs and this would make it easier for parents to care for their children whilst managing their work commitments.

sections.label: Preschool closure childcare leave
sections.summary: Preschool closures now reach up to eight working days a year, so existing childcare leave days are insufficient to cover closures, let alone illness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moreover, the reality is that parents will also need to care for their young children whenever their preschool closes, which according to the Early Childhood Development Agency, is now up to eight working days a year and increased from six days a year previously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: So, as it is, actually the existing childcare leave days are not even sufficient to cover for school closure days, let alone for when our children actually fall sick.

sections.label: Minimising parental pains and difficulties
sections.summary: It states that policies and legislation, including an incentive-disincentive framework for employers, can minimise pains and difficulties faced by parents and parents-to-be.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But what we can do is to minimise the pains and difficulties faced by parents and parents-to-be, just so that they can better see the joys and wonders of parenthood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And this is where we need to enact the right policies and legislation, putting in place something as simple as an incentive-disincentive framework for employers to make sure that fathers and mothers all take the full share of parental leave, they have sufficient leave to care for their child and that parents are not robbed of the ability to have FWAs just because of business needs.

sections.label: Total paid parental leave increase
sections.summary: When fully implemented on 1 April 2026, total paid parental leave will rise to 30 weeks from the current 20 weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: When fully implemented on 1 April 2026, it will bring total paid parental leave to 30 weeks, up from the current 20 weeks.

sections.label: Shared parenting and GPPL utilisation
sections.summary: It states that promoting shared parenting continues, but legislative support is futile if GPPL utilisation does not improve from 53% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We will also continue to keep up pace in evolving social-cultural norms by promoting the new norm of shared parenting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: But providing the legislative support is futile if the utilisation of the GPPL does not continue to improve from the 53% in 2022.

sections.label: Fines for errant employers
sections.summary: It states errant employers face a fine not exceeding $5,000 or up to six months' imprisonment, and asks about raising fines for first-time offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Errant employers are liable to a fine not exceeding $5,000 or up to a six-month term of imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry consider increasing the quantum of such a fine to not exceeding $10,000 for first-time offenders across GPML, GPPL and, in fact, adoption leave?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Over time, together with the upcoming Workplace Fairness Legislation, which will strengthen protections for employees with caregiving responsibilities against discrimination for all employment decisions, this will help to normalise the role of fathers in shouldering caregiving responsibilities.

sections.label: Family-oriented workplace policies benefits
sections.summary: It states that studies show supportive and family-oriented workplace policies enhance job satisfaction and may even enhance profitability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Yet, studies have also demonstrated that supportive and family-oriented workplace policies enhance job satisfaction and may even enhance profitability.

sections.label: Bill and gender pay gap
sections.summary: It states the Bill goes beyond shared caregiving responsibilities and can help narrow the gender pay gap and improve women's labour participation rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Bill before us today goes beyond addressing shared caregiving responsibilities alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: It can be a meaningful step towards narrowing the gender pay gap and improving the labour participation rates of women.

sections.label: Shared caregiving responsibilities between couples
sections.summary: The renewed GPPL aims to redistribute caregiving responsibilities more equitably at the start of a child's life, with hope this shared commitment endures during the child's formative years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: With the renewed GPPL aimed at redistributing caregiving responsibilities more equitably at the start of a child's life, I hope that this shared commitment between couples would endure during the child's formative years.

sections.label: CDCA Bill amendments and support
sections.summary: The Bill amends the CDCA to provide new SPL, double paid paternity leave to four weeks, and protect fathers from dismissal during paid paternity leave; PSP supported these changes to uplift Singapore's low TFR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Let us work together as a nation to champion supportive workplaces, encourage families for life and pave a way for a future where Singapore's sons and daughters live in a society that values their contributions equally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to amend the CDCA for several purposes, including providing for new SPL, doubling the total period of paid paternity leave to four weeks, and introducing protection for fathers against a notice of dismissal during paid paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In my response to the National Day Rally, I had stated that PSP supported these changes to uplift Singapore's low TFR, which fell to 0.97 in 2023.

sections.label: PSP supports CDCA Bill
sections.summary: PSP supports the CDCA Bill to provide four weeks of statutory paternal leave for working fathers and establish a new shared parental leave mechanism.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, Sir, PSP supports the CDCA Bill to provide four weeks of statutory paternal leave for working fathers as well as to establish a new shared parental leave mechanism.

sections.label: Costs and pro-family work culture
sections.summary: The Government must address high living costs and consider measures to encourage employers to create a more pro-family work culture to increase citizens' willingness to have children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: These include the cost of living, such as housing, healthcare and education, as well as job security and the employment environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We believe that if our country wants to further increase the willingness of citizens to have children, the Government must address the issue of high living costs and consider adopting measures to encourage employers to create a more pro-family work culture for their employees.

sections.label: Women's caregiving and workforce statistics
sections.summary: MOM statistics show about 260,000 women of economic age not in the workforce, and NTUC found women in dual-income families were five times more likely than men to manage housework and caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: According to the Ministry of Manpower's (MOM's) statistics, there are some 260,000 women of economic age who are not participating in the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Indeed, in the National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC's) #EveryWorkerMattersConversation Workers Compact Report in 2023, we found that in dual-income families, women were five times more likely than men to be managing housework and caregiving responsibilities, and women workers, unfortunately, were four times more likely to have left their jobs for caregiving than their men compatriots.

sections.label: Flexible Work Arrangement Guidelines implementation
sections.summary: The Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests will be implemented on 1 December this year, a move welcomed by parents and working caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests will be implemented on 1 December this year and our parents and working caregivers welcome this move.

sections.label: Workers prefer flexible work arrangements
sections.summary: In NTUC's engagement with 40,000 workers, 85% of workers with caregiving responsibilities cited FWAs as their most preferred support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In NTUC's engagement with 40,000 workers at our #EWMC Conversations, 85% of workers with caregiving responsibilities cited FWAs as their most preferred form of support.

sections.label: Enhanced parental leave for 2026 babies
sections.summary: A couple welcoming a baby in 2026 can get 30 weeks paid leave, with mandatory paternity leave doubled from two to four weeks.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Together with maternity leave, a couple who welcomes a baby in 2026 can benefit from 30 weeks of paid leave in total.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These enhancements that include the doubling of mandatory paternity leave from two to four weeks mark a major reset to policies and necessitate a major change in mindsets of how society can and should support parents and the parenting journey.

sections.label: Contract guidance for self-employed persons
sections.summary: Self-employed persons and service buyers are encouraged to negotiate mutually favourable contracts covering scenarios like pregnancy, referencing the Tripartite Standard.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Minister's response to the question provided the following guidance, "Self-employed persons and service buyers are encouraged to negotiate contracts that are mutually favourable, including providing for scenarios where a party is unable to fulfil the contract, such as pregnancy." Parties can take reference from the Tripartite Standard on contracting with self-employed persons and any disputes can be brought to the Small Claims Tribunal.

sections.label: Timing of GPML payout for freelancers
sections.summary: MSF is asked to consider paying GPML to eligible freelancers when maternity leave commences rather than after the ninth week.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On the operational aspect of the CDCA, given that the birth of a child is accompanied by many expenses, could MSF consider paying out the GPML amount to eligible freelancers when the maternity leave commences and not after the ninth week of the maternity leave period?

sections.label: Doubling paternity and shared parental leave
sections.summary: The Bill will double paid paternity leave to four weeks and introduce 10 weeks of shared parental leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With this Bill, we will double paid paternity leave to a total of four weeks and introduce 10 weeks of shared parental leave.

sections.label: Paternity leave take-up and caregiving poll
sections.summary: From 2018 to 2020 about 40% of eligible fathers took full GPPL, 2022 paternity leave take-up was 53%, and a 2022 poll found 68% wanted to be main caregivers but only 32% did.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: From 2018 to 2020, only about 40% of eligible fathers took the full two weeks of GPPL in each year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2022, the take-up rate for paternity leave stood at only 53%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: An online infant care poll in October 2022 by the Ministry of Digital Development and Information, found that 68% of respondents wanted themselves or their partners to be their infant's main caregiver but only 32% managed to make it happen.

sections.label: Tripartite partners and NGOs consultation
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister of State will look into this with tripartite partners and non-governmental organisations such as Families for Life and the Centre for Fathering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Minister of State look into this with tripartite partners and non-governmental oranisations, such as Families for Life and the Centre for Fathering?

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The passage states that if the time is missed it cannot be regained, expresses gratitude for more time with children, and supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If we miss it, we cannot get it back." I am grateful that the Government is providing more precious time for people to spend with their children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding these clarifications, Sir, I stand in support of the Bill.

sections.label: Guidance on reimbursement conditions
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry could provide clear guidance on reimbursement conditions to encourage companies to support new hires taking parental leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry provide clear guidance on the conditions for this reimbursement, as this could encourage more companies to adopt a progressive approach in supporting new hires in taking parental leave?

sections.label: Reimbursement for two part-time jobs
sections.summary: The passage asks how reimbursement limits and apportionment apply if a parent with two part-time jobs has combined claims exceeding the cap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, if a parent holds two part-time jobs, they are eligible to claim SPL leave from both employers, but how would reimbursement limits and apportionment apply if the combined claims exceed the cap?

sections.label: Clarity on reasonable cause for SMEs
sections.summary: The passage states that many SMEs will seek more clarity in defining reasonable cause so they can be in full compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many SMEs will be looking for more clarity in defining "reasonable cause", so that they can be in full compliance.

sections.label: Support measures for returning employees
sections.summary: The passage urges the Government to consider support measures such as extending pay coverage for returning employees by one to two months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To help manage these challenges, I urge the Government to strongly consider support measures, such as extending pay coverage for returning employees by one to two months, to help offset the operational impact.

sections.label: Parental leave weeks for parents
sections.summary: Four months maternity, four weeks paternity and 10 weeks shared parental leave give parents choice in balancing parenting and work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: By providing four months of maternity leave, four weeks of paternity leave and 10 weeks of SPL for a total of 30 weeks, we are giving moms and dads a genuine choice about how they want to balance parenting responsibilities and work.

sections.label: Discrimination caseload share in 2022
sections.summary: In 2022, such cases made up 85% of the service's entire discrimination caseload.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 2022, such cases made up 85% of the service’s entire discrimination caseload.

sections.label: Leave policy effects and discrimination protections
sections.summary: A study found a policy change cut women's employment and income, and the speaker urges stronger anti-discrimination protections for parental leave takers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A study found that the policy change caused a 30- percentage point decrease in women’s employment and a 2% to 4% decrease in income for employed women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Here, in Singapore, the Government is funding the increase in leave and the policy intent is for the leave to be taken by both men and women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to further ensure that protections against discrimination for those who take up any form of parental leave, whether it is SPL, GPPL or GPML are strengthened, possibly in the upcoming workplace fairness legislation.

sections.label: Shared parental leave and progress metrics
sections.summary: The speaker asks about half-day shared parental leave, calls for transparent metrics and surveys, and repeats a call to review childcare leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For shared parental leave, could it be taken rather than in full days, in half days and the time extended in order for companies to continue to be able to support their employers if needed?

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Thirdly, we must track and make transparent metrics that will help us measure our progress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We can regularly report headline metrics like take-up rates for the various forms of parental leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But beyond that, regular surveys can be done to measure shifts in culture and attitudes towards the ideal viz one where parenting is a more equal responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There should also be periodic assessments of the impact on workforce outcomes and birth rates to help us assess progress and make necessary corrections over time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Before I conclude, I would like to take the opportunity to repeat my call during the last Child Development Co-Savings (Amendment) Bill debate for the Government to also review childcare leave for families with many young children.

sections.label: Singapore total fertility rate decline
sections.summary: Minister Indranee told the House on 28 February 2024 that Singapore's TFR has declined and fallen below 1.0 for the first time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As shared by the Minister Indranee with this House on 28 February 2024, like many developed societies, Singapore's TFR has been on a declining trend and for the first time in history, fallen below 1.0.

sections.label: Attraction cost for family of six
sections.summary: A visit to a local attraction could cost a family of six around $450, and using the CDA would spare over half in cash.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Just as an example, while some local attractions offer subsidised rates or promotional offers for Singapore residents, a visit to one could cost this family of six, comprising two adults and four children, around $450.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: If allowed to tap on the CDA, it would spare them from having to cough out more than half in cash.

sections.label: Take-up rate at 53%
sections.summary: The take-up rate has risen steadily in recent years but is still at 53%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: While the take-up rate has risen steadily in recent years, it is still at 53%.

sections.label: Notice period and parental leave queries
sections.summary: A member asks about flexibility for premature births and whether other countries' parental leave measures were referenced.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Under this Bill, there is a requirement of a new minimum notice period of four weeks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: While I can understand that this is to help employers better adjust their operations after parental leave benefits are enhanced, because parents may leave work for some time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: However, as we all know, the journey of pregnancy may be rather unexpected, with occasional instances of premature births that may happen despite parents' best-laid plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In such instances, may I ask whether there is a flexibility in how this law is being enforced and what level of support is available to alleviate or waive such notice periods? : Finally, when allocating the appropriate length of paid parental leaves for the mother and father respectively, as well as shared parental leave, I wish to enquire with the Ministry, whether the Government had taken reference from the measures introduced or enhanced by other countries – beyond those of the UK and US, as shared by the Minister of State Sun Xueling earlier – to better support their citizens in embracing parenthood?

sections.label: Maternity leave beyond parenting
sections.summary: A member asks Mr Louis Ng whether he recognises that maternity leave is not just about parenting and childcare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I had not meant to speak on this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But on hon Member Mr Louis Ng's point about equalisation of parental leave – as for in maternity and paternity leave – I totally agree with him that we should in-step move towards that, because the joint involvement of both parents is very important for child development and care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But he was so adamant on this, so, I want to ask him this clarification because he kept talking about maternity leave and paternity leave and childcaring and child rearing, which is important.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I just want to ask him this clarification: does he recognise that maternity leave is not just about parenting and childcare?

sections.label: Fathers' time for mothers' recovery
sections.summary: A member says fathers should be given time because mothers need to recover from childbirth, and raised extending parental leave for multiples and pre-term babies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker was smiling quite a bit, so it worried me for quite a while, but I knew she was going to put her hand up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: It is precisely because the mother needs to recover from childbirth that the father needs to be there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Sometimes, of course, you can outsource it to the helper, but it is precisely that the mothers need to recover from childbirth, that is why we should give fathers the time to be there for the mother and for the children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I had raised this in my Adjournment Motion as well for extending parental leave for those with multiples – twins as well as pre-term babies.

sections.label: Amendments to parental leave framework
sections.summary: The proposed amendments update the existing framework to increase support for working parents, expand parental leave options and extend coverage to diverse family structures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments introduce key updates to the existing framework, aimed at increasing support for working parents, expanding options for parental leave and extending coverage to diverse family structures.

sections.label: Support for self-employed parents
sections.summary: The Bill provides income loss compensation for self-employed parents and accommodates dual employment scenarios.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: With the rise in self-employment and concurrent employment arrangements, it is essential that our family support policies adapt.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Thus, this Bill provides income loss compensation for self-employed parents and accommodates unique scenarios like dual employment, ensuring no family is left behind.

sections.label: Support measures for SMEs
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Government to consider subsidised administrative support, a helpline or advisory service, and a streamlined parental leave reimbursement process for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: To support SMEs in fulfilling these commitments, I ask that the Government consider several measures, including subsidised administrative support, a dedicated helpline or advisory service, and a streamlined reimbursement process for parental leave.

sections.label: Six-day childcare leave entitlement
sections.summary: The six-day childcare leave entitlement is helpful but may fall short for parents with multiple children or frequent health or school demands.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: At present, the six-day childcare leave entitlement is helpful, yet it may fall short, for parents with multiple children or for those who face frequent health or school-related demands.

sections.label: Shared parental leave amendments
sections.summary: The amendments introduce a shared parental leave scheme, financial assistance to self-employed parents and flexibility, and the speaker urges addressing workplace stigma against parents taking extended leave.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments will introduce a shared parental leave scheme, provide financial assistance to self-employed parents and offer flexibility to families in different employment situations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Additionally, I also urge us to address workplace stigma against parents who take extended leave to care for their children.

sections.label: Bill builds caring society
sections.summary: The Bill is a positive step towards a more caring society supporting families in Singapore and a more supportive and inclusive Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Overall, this Bill is a positive step towards building a more caring society that support families in Singapore. : Mr Speaker, the Bill represents a significant step forward in building a more supportive and inclusive Singapore for our families.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: Notwithstanding the concerns raised, the speaker supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the concerns raised, I support the Bill.

sections.label: Eligibility and Shared Parental Leave Benefit
sections.summary: Employees must serve the employer continuously for at least three months before the child's birth; those not meeting this may qualify for the Shared Parental Leave Benefit if they worked at least 90 days in the last 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: One of the eligibility criteria is that the employee should serve the employer for a continuous period of at least three months before the child's birth, to be entitled to take this paid leave with the employer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Working parents who do not meet the minimum employment period of three months, such as those whose babies are born shortly after joining the company, may qualify for the new Shared Parental Leave Benefit scheme instead if they have worked at least 90 days in the last 12 months.

sections.label: Penalties for denying parental leave
sections.summary: Penalties apply only when employers fail to show reasonable cause for not granting parental leave within 12 months after birth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The penalties will only apply when employers fail to demonstrate with reasonable cause that they could not grant parental leave at any time during the 12 months after the child's birth.

sections.label: Reimbursement cap for shared parental leave
sections.summary: Government reimbursement and direct payment for paid leave is capped at $2,500 per week, with employers reimbursed before self-employed parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: For example, for the new SPL, the total amount that the Government may reimburse the parent’s employers for paid leave given to the parent and pay directly to the parent as a self-employed person will be capped at $2,500 per week.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: If the total reimbursement across multiple employments exceeds $2,500 per week, the Government will reimburse the parent’s employers first, as employers would have already paid for their employee’s leave, before considering claims by the parent as a self-employed person.

sections.label: Employers recovering excess claim amounts
sections.summary: The Bill lets employers recover the difference directly from employees if the total claim exceeds the reimbursement limit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The Bill provides for employers to recover the difference directly from their employees, if the total claim amount exceeds the reimbursement limit.

sections.label: Paying fathers' paternity and parental leave
sections.summary: Fathers get protection from dismissal, and both leave types are paid in full up to $2,500 per week or about $10,000 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In response to Mr Louis Ng's point on incentivising fathers to take paternity leave and shared parental leave, not only are we offering fathers protection from dismissal, we are also paying for both types of leave in full up to $2,500 per week or about $10,000 per month.

sections.label: Preschool closure days and childcare leave
sections.summary: The net increase was 0.5 days of preschool closure, not two additional days as the Member thought.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: To Mr Louis Chua’s suggestion to increase Childcare Leave from six to eight days in view of the additional preschool closure days, I would like to clarify that there has been a net increase of 0.5 days of preschool closure and not two additional days as the Member had thought.

sections.label: Doubled unpaid infant care leave
sections.summary: Unpaid Infant Care Leave was doubled to 12 days per parent in the child's first two years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: At the start of this year, we also doubled Unpaid Infant Care Leave to 12 days per parent in the child’s first two years.

sections.label: Government-paid parental leave provisions
sections.summary: Most Singapore parental leave provisions are paid by the Government at $2,500 per week or about $10,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Indeed, one key approach is that most of Singapore's parental leave provisions are paid by the Government and at a generous level of $2,500 per week or about $10,000 per month.

sections.label: Employer reimbursement commitment
sections.summary: The Government is committed to timely reimbursements to employers and streamlining claim processes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On the Government's reimbursement to employers, I would like to assure Dr Wan Rizal that we are committed to ensuring timely reimbursements and streamlining the claim processes.

sections.label: Baby Bonus and CDA enhancements
sections.summary: The Baby Bonus cash gift and Government contributions to the CDA were enhanced last year to help defray child-raising costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In particular, we recognise that parents may be concerned about the cost of raising children, as several Members have highlighted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We recently enhanced the Baby Bonus cash gift and Government contributions to the CDA, last year, to support parents in defraying the cost of child-raising.

sections.label: Caregiving support and family commitment
sections.summary: The Bill's amendments support working parents in their child's early years, and parenthood continues beyond infancy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The current amendments covered in this Bill are part of the Government's commitment to better provide working parents with greater caregiving support, especially in their child's early years when the care needs are the greatest.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We hope that both mothers and fathers will use the enhanced leave provisions well, to bond with their children and share the parenthood journey together.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We must also recognise that these schemes do not operate in isolation and that parenthood continues beyond infancy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We will, therefore, need to press on with our whole-of-society effort to build a Singapore Made For Families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Are there any clarifications for the Minister of State Sun Xueling?

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I still recall that when I became a Member of Parliament in 2006, GPML was significantly lower than what it is now.
